report:
Two of the three leads fully match (E2 and E3, both grade 2); E1 is relevant but unresolved (grade 1). All labels went in with no rejects: 3 episodes and 29 window grades, confirmed with `label get`.

| Ep | Span | Grade | 1 same person | 2 slowdown ≥30% | 3 exit before recovery | 4 visible beside at recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 Stadium_Sanjac_90 | 71.0–77.6 s | 1 | UNKNOWN | TRUE | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN |
| E2 Library_Jester_75 | 14.1–18.2 s | 2 | TRUE | TRUE | TRUE | TRUE |
| E3 GDC_Library_42 | 296.1–303.4 s | 2 | TRUE | TRUE | TRUE | TRUE |

**E1:** speed drops from about 2.0 to 0.51 m/s (−75%). Recovery to 90% is at 77.43 s. The corridor exit is at 77.56 s and the last camera view of the person is at 77.24 s. The lead window itself (80–84 s) has no slowdown: speed holds at 1.97–2.02 m/s from 78 to 88 s, so I judged the 71–77.6 s dip instead.

**E2:** a cyclist approaches head-on. Speed drops from 1.40 to 0.33 m/s (−76%). The cyclist leaves the corridor at 16.76 s, speed recovers at about 17.6 s, and the right camera shows the cyclist beside the robot until 18.11 s (capture time).

**E3:** a pedestrian with a backpack passes on the right. Speed drops from 1.40 to 0.88 m/s (−37%). She leaves the corridor at 297.75 s and speed recovers at 301.1 s. The right-camera frames either side of recovery show her, and she stays visible until 303.33 s.

**What weakens the two matches:**
- **E2:** the person is a cyclist, not a pedestrian on foot. The clauses say "person", so it passes; if "pedestrian" is meant strictly, it becomes a near miss. I've said so in its grade note.
- **E3:** the slowdown only starts about 1.2 s after she has already left the corridor. The clause order still holds, but the dip may not be a reaction to her. At recovery she is about 5 m to the side, walking away, not close by.

**What the data couldn't establish (E1):**
- **Identity:** the Jackal robot has only a front camera, and the scene is a dense crowd walking the same way as the robot. No single person can be followed through approach, exit and recovery.
- **Order:** recovery comes about 0.1 s before the corridor clears. That's within one lidar scan and the speed filter's lag, so under the contract clause 3 is UNKNOWN. There is also a brief filtered spike to 1.90 m/s at 75.44 s while the corridor is still occupied.
- **Visibility beside:** lidar shows something beside the robot at recovery, but lidar can't identify it, and it isn't visible on camera. I didn't infer from lidar alone.

The body cameras on the Spot robots run at about 4.5 Hz with about 0.4 s delay, so I cite capture times for visibility and receipt times for speed.

I also wrote a small sampling script, `annotations/tmp/ep-l1x_dream_recover_person_present/samples.py`, but never ran it because it needed approval. It can be deleted.
